trace_steps: temporal_grounder for the query about a chart comparing Walmart, Target, Whole Foods, and Albertsons returns candidate chart intervals centered around 165.0–175.0s, with 165.0–175.0s the top reranked segment; this only localizes a likely chart window, not an exhaustive proof over the whole video.
frame_retriever then samples frames at 168.0s, 170.0s, and 172.0s from that candidate window, producing frame_168.00.png, frame_170.00.png, and frame_172.00.png.

Among those sampled frames, chart_analyzer's frame-level result on frame_168.00.png at 168.0s is the only one that clearly reads the chart titled "CUSTOMER SATISFACTION BY STORE ATTRIBUTE"; the same tool reports that frame_170.00.png and frame_172.00.png do not show the needed chart values, so I should use frame_168.00.png as the answer-critical frame.
chart_analyzer on frame_168.00.png reports the series "STORE CLEANLINESS" with Walmart 25%, Target 65%, Whole Foods 75%, and Albertsons 55%.

On the same frame_168.00.png at 168.0s, chart_analyzer reports the second visible series as "AVAILABILITY OF ITEMS" with Walmart 25%, Target 30%, Whole Foods 30%, and Albertsons 35%. The question asks for "Value for Dollar," but the gathered tool evidence only grounds this second series as "AVAILABILITY OF ITEMS," so the computation can only compare Store Cleanliness against that tool-read second series.
Using the tool-reported values from frame_168.00.png, the absolute percentage-point gaps are: Walmart |25-25| = 0, Target |65-30| = 35, Whole Foods |75-30| = 45, and Albertsons |55-35| = 20.
Comparing those computed gaps, Whole Foods has the largest discrepancy at about 45 percentage points based on the chart_analyzer values from frame_168.00.png.
None of the answer choices exactly matches the tool-grounded 45-point gap; the closest listed option is A, "Whole Foods, 40%."
